item.title: Apple says it’s ‘hard to predict’ when iPhone Duo constraints will improve
item.dc:creator: Sarah Perez
item.description: Apple says iPhone Duo production is ramping up, but it still can't say when supply will catch up with demand as shipping delays stretch into next year.

item.title: Trajectory raises $45M to make AI model training accessible to nontechnical experts
item.dc:creator: Marina Temkin
item.description: The one-year-old startup is now valued at $300 million.

item.title: Apple’s inventory surges 154% as memory chip costs climb
item.dc:creator: Sarah Perez
item.description: Apple says unprecedented memory chip costs will continue to rise, raising questions about future device prices as its inventory climbs to $14.5 billion.

item.title: Anthropic warns that it’s very close to RSI capability, aka self-building AI
item.dc:creator: Julie Bort
item.description: RSI is the point at which AI grows so good at training itself that it spawns a dramatic acceleration of AI capabilities. To the AI doomers, RSI represents the cataclysm from which there is no return.

item.title: Germany says lawmakers’ iPhones may have been hacked with spyware
item.dc:creator: Zack Whittaker
item.description: German lawmakers and a filmmaker are among the people who received notifications from Apple warning that their phones may have been hacked.

item.title: Web host Squarespace lays off 19% of its employees
item.dc:creator: Lucas Ropek
item.description: The website builder said that the job losses are part of a broader restructuring of its organization.

item.title: New York Times and other outlets sue web browser Brave over alleged content scraping
item.dc:creator: Rebecca Bellan
item.description: The New York Times is suing privacy-focused web browser company Brave for allegedly scraping the outlet’s copyrighted content and unlawfully distributing it to its own customers, like Anthropic and Perplexity.

item.title: Snap settles lawsuit accusing platform of fueling teen depression and eating disorders
item.dc:creator: Aisha Malik
item.description: The plaintiffs said they started using YouTube as young as age 3 and other social media platforms at around age 9 and developed compulsive usage habits that they attributed to features such as autoplay and infinite scrolling.

item.title: In one of the largest deals in tech history, Marvell buys Lumentum for $115B
item.dc:creator: Julie Bort
item.description: Marvell's planned purchase of Lumentum is one of the biggest acquisitions in tech history. And they both have the same strategic investor: Nvidia.

item.title: Readwise takes on Amazon’s Kindle and Goodreads with its new app for book lovers
item.dc:creator: Sarah Perez
item.description: Readwise Books combines an e-book store, reading tracker, detailed reading stats, and AI features in a bid to challenge Amazon's ecosystem.

item.title: SpaceX reportedly wants to buy Boost Mobile to compete with AT&T, T-Mobile, and Verizon
item.dc:creator: Tim De Chant

item.title: 42AI comes out of stealth with $62.5M and a world model that can ‘predict human behavior’
item.dc:creator: Ram Iyer
item.description: Here's a question straight out of sci-fi: What if AI could predict what you were going to do before you decided to, even in a completely new situation?

item.title: Elon Musk throttles Grok Bot limits due to ‘unsustainably high’ costs
item.dc:creator: Amanda Silberling

item.title: Omen AI adds liquid know-how in $16 million Aquatic Labs acquisition
